avenue.songTitle: Christmas Card from a Hooker in Minneapolis
avenue.line: Right above a dirty bookstore off Euclid Avenue
stanza: Hey Charlie, I'm pregnant and living on 9th Street
Right above a dirty bookstore off Euclid Avenue
And I stopped takin' dope, and I quit drinkin' whiskey
And my old man plays the trombone and works out at the track
Asking only workman's wages
I come looking for a job
But I get no offers
Just a come-on from the whores
On Seventh Avenue
I do declare
There were times when I was so
Lonesome
I took some comfort there
I broke free on a Saturday morning
I put the pedal to the floor
Headed north on Mills Avenue
And listened to the engine roar

bellevue.line: Fuckin' with them corners have a nigga up in Bellevue
bellevue.linePrev: You see the streets had me stressed somethin' terrible
bellevue.lineNext: Or HDM, hit with numbers from eight to ten

stanza: I don't want to hold you and feel so helpless
I don't want to smell you and lose my senses
And smile in slow motion
With eyes in love
I twist like a corkscrew
The sweetness rising
I drink from the bottle, weeping
Why won't you last?
Why can't you last?

guru.line: He's a ghost, he's a god, he's a man, he's a guru
stanza: He'll wrap you up in his arms, tell you that you've been good girls and boys
He'll rekindle all of those dreams it took you a lifetime to destroy
He'll reach deep into the hole, heal your shrinking soul
Mm, but people, you know you're never coming back
He's a ghost, he's a god, he's a man, he's a guru
We're whispering his name through this disappearing land
But hidden in his coat is a red right hand

hulu.line: Little fuckers fighting, mother hiding in her Hulu
hulu.linePrev: Woo him with the Schubert, he's a future human cannonball
hulu.lineNext: I'm climbing up the stucco, let's get to the seppuku—uh-oh

stanza: Cross twelve letters down, found the longest word
This morning, I'd heard
Somebody said they saw you 'round 1st and 23rd
Blue feathers in your hairdo

honeydew.line: You were full and sweet as honeydew
stanza: Now we arise to curse those young suburban villains
And their ill-begotten children from the lawn
Come to me now, and on this station wagon window
Set the ghost of your two footprints
That they might haunt me when you're gone
And when the light broke dawn, you were forever gone
But I remember you: you were full
You were full and sweet as honeydew
